messages:
Anya: Heads up – triage: exporter instability during scale tests. Proposal: add connection leasing and a lightweight retry journal in the OTLP exporter to ensure idempotent retries and controlled conn reuse. Thoughts?

Sam: +1 on controlled conn reuse. We saw thrashing when many processes reconnect after deploy. Pool of N per process sounds right.

Leo: How does leasing differ from a simple pool? Leasing = short-lived borrow + lease TTL, release back to pool. Helps draining on shutdown and prevents hot-connection stickiness.

Maria: Concern: gRPC keepalive + long-lived connections help throughput but cause hot connections to linger on node kill. Leasing helps graceful eviction. Also we need idempotency for span export to avoid dupes during retry.

Anya: Exactly. Idea: exporter keeps a lease_token per RPC. On retry we consult a retry-journal (recent window) keyed by (resource, span_batch_hash) to dedupe. Journal is in-memory ring buffer per process, bounded to avoid OOM.

Sam: Implementation Q: journal size vs retention. We saw spikes when batching window is large. Suggest journal TTL = max_retry_window + 2s. Make it configurable.

Leo: We should also emit telemetry: journal_hits, journal_misses, leased_conns, lease_waiters, lease_acquire_latency. Add to exporter metrics so SRE can alert.

Anya: Proposed config snippet:

```yaml
otlp_exporter:
  protocol: grpc
  conn_lease:
    pool_size: 3
    lease_ttl: 5s
    wait_timeout: 200ms
  retry:
    max_retries: 4
    initial_backoff: 100ms
    max_backoff: 4s
  retry_journal:
    enabled: true
    ttl: 10s
    max_entries: 5000
```

Sam: Nice. Also add protocol_fallback: true so exporter can try http if grpc dial fails (short-circuit for transient network failures).

Maria: Add drain semantics on SIGTERM: stop issuing new leases, mark instance draining, wait for active leases up to 10s, flush journal, then shutdown. Deploy tooling should mark nodes as draining earlier in rollout.

deploy-bot: @here Starting node drain stage will now annotate instances with drain=true 60s before SIGTERM for canaries and 30s for rolling.

Leo: Edge cases: when conn pool is exhausted and waiters pile up — do we block or fail-fast? For our tail latency SLOs, fail-fast with a small retry budget seems better. Queueing here will amplify P99.

Anya: Agree. We'll default to fail-fast (wait_timeout=200ms) and expose config. Also add a per-route retry_budget hook later. For now add metrics and dashboards.

Sam: Regarding idempotency key: can we reuse span identifiers? Some spans have variable attributes. Better to compute a stable 64-bit hash of the serialized batch (no raw payload stored).

Maria: Security note: do not store raw spans or attributes in the journal (PII risk). Store only the hash + timestamp + small metadata.

Leo: I'll prototype on branch exporter_kv: implement lease manager + inproc journal + metrics. Will add unit tests and an integration run against local collector.

Anya: I'll join for integration tomorrow 10:00 PT to exercise drain + failover flows. Thanks all :thumbsup:
